qa.sample_note: nothing was sampled. Read by hand: all 21 same-notation accent variants, the 6 weakest accepted near parallels, the 16 top-of-sample 'random' pairs that disproved the naive floor calibration, the 6 sub-threshold svaha identities, the codepoint diff of the 475 orthographic variants, the per-veda-pair ceiling reachability table, every difference class of the 158 apparatus rows, and the five length outliers per Veda that decided whether length is a commentary detector.
defects: THE CLASSIFIER HANDLED ONE INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS. The comparison ceiling was fixed by a digit exception after the adversarial preflight; the owner ruled that not importable. A structural reference is a CLASS -- self-address, section labels, edition apparatus, embedded citation language -- and the digit branch could not reach 24 rows it left typed as edition variants, including 18 Samavedic pairs whose whole difference is ASCII '|' against a Devanagari danda. Rebuilt as a general rule with no per-pair exception.

MY FIRST STRIPPER WAS DESTRUCTIVE. It cut the text at any citation marker; in SV ARANYA 1.4 the marker sits in a prefix, so cutting at 'bhasyam' deleted 107 characters that were the mantra. Rules now carry position conditions, plus a 40%-strip guard and an assertion that no mantra is made uncomparable.

MY FIRST CLASS-5 DETECTOR READ ACCENTS AS CHANGED WORDING. It decomposed the difference at UNICODE_NORMALIZED, so for a cross-script pair every character differed; the invariant 'no exact row touches true wording' fired 284 times. Class 5 is now derived from the pair's own ceiling and the invariant holds by construction.
the comparison ceiling was missing a third axis (the adversarial preflight; 134 rows).
the first digit-only probe ignored whitespace, which would have moved 12 WORD_DIVISION pairs whose real difference is a space.
the first difference class lumped digits with dandas, which would have moved 18 Samavedic rows containing no digit at all.
the 6 sub-threshold svaha rows carried a hard-coded match_level; 5 of 6 were wrong.
1,475 VARIANT rows shipped with evidence quoting the surface on which the two texts AGREE.
claim_confidence read NOT_APPLICABLE on 4,103 rows that make a claim.
the first transformation typology special-cased accent notation instead of deriving a ceiling.

I RAN THE GATE FIVE TIMES WHILE REWRITING THE FILES IT READS. Every one reported manifest.file_checksums 28/28 against a shipped manifest listing 29, so each described a mixture of old and new bytes rather than the artifact. All five are withdrawn; the verdict of record is a run started 8 seconds after the last write on a frozen directory, 29/29 checksums, PASS. See proofs/validation_race_and_the_verdict_of_record.json. The rule this should have followed: generate the manifest LAST, write nothing between it and the validation that covers it, and read the checksum count rather than the word PASS.

the first false-duplicate test compared structural_path, which is null for the Rigveda, so all 252 RV pairs returned SAME_ADDRESS_INGESTION_DUPLICATE while the printed examples showed different mandalas. A null-equals-null comparison is not a match.

the first near-parallel floor calibration read the random-pair maximum as a null maximum and concluded the imported 0.72 floor was unsafe on the YV and AV. Reading the tail showed every high-scoring 'random' pair is a genuine near parallel -- the sample was contaminated by real signal, which is what a repetitive corpus does to random sampling. Had the number been accepted, a threshold would have been invented to fit it.
